---
title: "Urban to Forest Gradient"
subtitle: "Annual NLCD land cover, impervious surface, and leaf-off NDVI along the transect"
date: today
---

```{r setup}
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(leaflet)
library(terra)
library(here)

source(here("R", "functions.R"))
derived <- here(cfg$paths$derived)

line    <- load_transect()
aoi     <- load_aoi()
windows <- load_windows()
nlcd    <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "nlcd_windows.csv"))
classes <- read.csv(file.path(derived, "nlcd_window_classes.csv"))
lc      <- rast(here(cfg$nlcd$dir, sprintf("LndCov_%d.tif", cfg$nlcd$year)))

ndvi_path <- file.path(derived, "ndvi_windows.csv")
ndvi <- if (file.exists(ndvi_path)) read.csv(ndvi_path) else NULL

# Join on the window id only; the distance columns are floats and may not match exactly
windows <- left_join(windows, select(nlcd, -u_start_km, -u_end_km, -u_mid_km, -area_km2), by = "window")
if (!is.null(ndvi)) windows <- left_join(windows, select(ndvi, -u_mid_km), by = "window")

# Grouped cover, ordered from most to least urban; colors follow the NLCD legend
cover_cols <- c(
  developed      = "#eb0000",
  developed_open = "#dec5c5",
  barren         = "#b3ac9f",
  agriculture    = "#dcd939",
  shrub_grass    = "#ccb879",
  forest         = "#38814e",
  wetland        = "#b8d9eb",
  water          = "#466b9f"
)
cover_labels <- c(
  developed = "Developed (low to high)", developed_open = "Developed, open space",
  barren = "Barren", agriculture = "Agriculture", shrub_grass = "Shrub and grassland",
  forest = "Forest", wetland = "Wetland", water = "Water"
)
```

## Purpose

A first look at how land use changes from downtown Richmond to Pocahontas State Park.
The study area is cut into non-overlapping 1 km windows along the transect, each spanning
the full 4 km buffer width, and each window is summarized from the
[Annual NLCD](https://www.usgs.gov/centers/eros/science/annual-national-land-cover-database)
`r cfg$nlcd$year` land cover and fractional impervious surface layers (30 m) and from NDVI
computed from the 4-band (RGB + near-infrared) 12-inch imagery.

| Step | Script | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 5. Transect windows | `R/04_transect_windows.R` | `data/derived/transect_windows.gpkg` |
| 6. NLCD download and window summaries | `R/05_nlcd.R` | `data/raw/nlcd/*.tif`, `data/derived/nlcd_windows.csv`, `nlcd_window_classes.csv` |
| 9. NDVI window summaries | `R/07_ndvi_windows.R` | `data/derived/ndvi_10ft.tif`, `ndvi_windows.csv`, `ndvi_calibration.csv` |

NLCD is kept on its native grid (EPSG:5070). Windows are projected to it and summarized
with `exactextractr`, which weights each 30 m cell by the fraction of it inside the window.

## Windows

```{r window-summary}
n_win <- nrow(windows)
```

- **Windows:** `r n_win`, each `r cfg$windows$length_km` km long by `r 2 * cfg$buffer$half_width_km` km wide
  (the last is `r sprintf("%.2f", tail(windows$length_km, 1))` km)
- **Area covered:** `r sprintf("%.1f", sum(windows$area_km2))` of `r sprintf("%.1f", as.numeric(aoi$area_km2))` km².
  The round end caps beyond the endpoints are not part of any window.
- Window 1 is at the Richmond end. Distance along the transect (*u*, km) is measured from
  the Richmond endpoint; `transect_position()` in `R/functions.R` returns *u*, the signed
  lateral offset *v*, and the window id for any point.

Use the layer control (top right) to choose which value colors the windows; hover a window
for all of its values.

```{r map-leaflet}
to_ll <- function(x) st_transform(x, 4326)
win_ll <- to_ll(windows)
win_ll$label <- sprintf(
  "<b>Window %d</b> (%.0f–%.0f km)<br>Impervious: %.1f%%<br>Developed: %.1f%%<br>
   Developed, open: %.1f%%<br>Forest: %.1f%%<br>Wetland + water: %.1f%%",
  win_ll$window, win_ll$u_start_km, win_ll$u_end_km, win_ll$imperv_mean, win_ll$developed_pct,
  win_ll$developed_open_pct, win_ll$forest_pct, win_ll$wetland_pct + win_ll$water_pct
)
win_ll$wet_water <- win_ll$wetland_pct + win_ll$water_pct
if (!is.null(ndvi)) {
  win_ll$label <- paste0(win_ll$label, sprintf("<br>Evergreen (NDVI): %.1f%%", win_ll$evg_pct))
}

# One single-hue sequential scale per metric, all on a shared 0-100% domain
metrics <- list(
  "Impervious surface" = list(col = "imperv_mean",   pal = "Purples"),
  "Developed"          = list(col = "developed_pct", pal = "Reds"),
  "Forest"             = list(col = "forest_pct",    pal = "Greens"),
  "Wetland + water"    = list(col = "wet_water",     pal = "Blues")
)
if (!is.null(ndvi)) metrics[["Evergreen (NDVI)"]] <- list(col = "evg_pct", pal = "BuGn")

m <- leaflet(win_ll) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery, group = "Imagery")
for (nm in names(metrics)) {
  pal <- colorNumeric(metrics[[nm]]$pal, domain = c(0, 100))
  m <- m |>
    addPolygons(color = "white", weight = 1, fillOpacity = 0.7,
                fillColor = pal(win_ll[[metrics[[nm]]$col]]),
                label = lapply(win_ll$label, htmltools::HTML),
                highlightOptions = highlightOptions(color = "black", weight = 2, bringToFront = TRUE),
                group = nm) |>
    addLegend(pal = pal, values = c(0, 100), title = paste(nm, "(%)"),
              position = "bottomright", className = "info legend metric-legend",
              layerId = nm)
}
m |>
  addPolylines(data = to_ll(line), color = "black", dashArray = "6", weight = 2) |>
  addLayersControl(baseGroups = names(metrics), overlayGroups = "Imagery",
                   options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) |>
  hideGroup("Imagery") |>
  # Leaflet does not hide legends for radio (base) layers; show only the selected metric's
  htmlwidgets::onRender(sprintf("
    function(el, x) {
      var map = this;
      function show(name) {
        el.querySelectorAll('.metric-legend').forEach(function(lg) {
          lg.style.display = lg.textContent.trim().startsWith(name + ' (%%)') ? '' : 'none';
        });
      }
      show(%s);
      map.on('baselayerchange', function(e) { show(e.name); });
    }", jsonlite::toJSON(names(metrics)[1], auto_unbox = TRUE)))
```

## Land cover

```{r lc-map, fig.width=7, fig.height=8}
nlcd_names <- c(
  `11` = "Open water", `21` = "Developed, open space", `22` = "Developed, low",
  `23` = "Developed, medium", `24` = "Developed, high", `31` = "Barren",
  `41` = "Deciduous forest", `42` = "Evergreen forest", `43` = "Mixed forest",
  `52` = "Shrub/scrub", `71` = "Grassland", `81` = "Pasture/hay", `82` = "Cultivated crops",
  `90` = "Woody wetlands", `95` = "Emergent wetlands"
)
aoi_lc <- vect(st_transform(aoi, crs(lc)))
lc_aoi <- mask(crop(lc, aoi_lc), aoi_lc)
present <- sort(unique(values(lc_aoi, na.rm = TRUE)[, 1]))
levels(lc_aoi) <- data.frame(value = present, class = nlcd_names[as.character(present)])
plot(lc_aoi, mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 12), axes = FALSE,
     plg = list(cex = 0.8))
plot(vect(st_transform(windows, crs(lc))), add = TRUE, border = "grey20", lwd = 0.5)
plot(vect(st_transform(line, crs(lc))), add = TRUE, col = "black", lty = 2)
```

## Gradient

The charts below are interactive: hover to read every value at one distance, click a legend
entry to hide it (double-click to show it alone), and drag to zoom (double-click to reset).
Lines connect window midpoints, so values between midpoints are interpolated.

```{r plotly-setup}
library(plotly)

# Shared x axis and landmarks
river_km  <- nlcd$u_mid_km[which.max(nlcd$water_pct)]
end_km    <- max(nlcd$u_end_km)
x_axis <- list(title = "Distance from Richmond (km)", range = c(0, end_km),
               dtick = 5, zeroline = FALSE, showgrid = FALSE)
landmarks <- list(
  list(x = 0, y = 1.02, yref = "paper", text = "Richmond", showarrow = FALSE,
       xanchor = "left", yanchor = "bottom", font = list(size = 12)),
  list(x = end_km, y = 1.02, yref = "paper", text = "Pocahontas State Park", showarrow = FALSE,
       xanchor = "right", yanchor = "bottom", font = list(size = 12)),
  list(x = river_km, y = 1.02, yref = "paper", text = "James River", showarrow = FALSE,
       yanchor = "bottom", font = list(size = 12, color = "#466b9f"))
)
river_line <- list(type = "line", x0 = river_km, x1 = river_km, y0 = 0, y1 = 1,
                   yref = "paper", line = list(color = "#466b9f", width = 1, dash = "dot"))
plotly_cfg <- function(p) {
  config(p, displaylogo = FALSE,
         modeBarButtonsToRemove = c("lasso2d", "select2d", "autoScale2d"))
}
```

### Land cover composition

Share of each window in each grouped cover type. Developed land is stacked from the bottom
and forest above it, so the urban-to-forest transition reads as the green band widening
toward Pocahontas State Park.

```{r cover-area}
p <- plot_ly()
for (k in names(cover_cols)) {
  p <- add_trace(p, data = nlcd, x = ~u_mid_km, y = nlcd[[paste0(k, "_pct")]],
                 type = "scatter", mode = "lines", stackgroup = "cover",
                 name = cover_labels[[k]], fillcolor = cover_cols[[k]],
                 line = list(color = "white", width = 0.5),
                 hovertemplate = paste0(cover_labels[[k]], ": %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>"))
}
p |>
  layout(xaxis = c(x_axis, list(hoverformat = ".1f")),
         yaxis = list(title = "Share of window (%)", range = c(0, 100), ticksuffix = "%"),
         hovermode = "x unified",
         legend = list(traceorder = "reversed"),
         annotations = landmarks, shapes = list(river_line),
         margin = list(t = 40)) |>
  plotly_cfg()
```

### Impervious surface and forest

Mean fractional impervious surface and forest cover per window. The shaded band is ± 1 SD of
impervious surface among the 30 m cells in each window, a measure of how mixed the window is.

```{r imperv-forest}
imp_col <- "#5e3c99"
for_col <- "#38814e"
band <- nlcd |> mutate(lo = pmax(imperv_mean - imperv_sd, 0), hi = pmin(imperv_mean + imperv_sd, 100))

plot_ly(band, x = ~u_mid_km) |>
  add_ribbons(ymin = ~lo, ymax = ~hi, name = "Impervious ± 1 SD",
              fillcolor = "rgba(94, 60, 153, 0.15)", line = list(width = 0),
              hovertemplate = "Impervious ± 1 SD: %{customdata}<extra></extra>",
              customdata = ~sprintf("%.0f–%.0f%%", lo, hi)) |>
  add_trace(y = ~imperv_mean, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers", name = "Impervious surface",
            line = list(color = imp_col, width = 2), marker = list(color = imp_col, size = 8),
            hovertemplate = "Impervious surface: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>") |>
  add_trace(y = ~forest_pct, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers", name = "Forest",
            line = list(color = for_col, width = 2), marker = list(color = for_col, size = 8),
            hovertemplate = "Forest: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>") |>
  layout(xaxis = c(x_axis, list(hoverformat = ".1f")),
         yaxis = list(title = "Percent", range = c(0, 100), ticksuffix = "%"),
         hovermode = "x unified",
         legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2),
         annotations = landmarks, shapes = list(river_line),
         margin = list(t = 40)) |>
  plotly_cfg()
```

### Evergreen signal (NDVI)

```{r ndvi-text, eval=!is.null(ndvi), results="asis"}
cat(sprintf(
"The imagery was flown leaf-off, so near-infrared greenness mostly marks evergreen foliage
(pine, cedar, holly, magnolia, evergreen shrubs) and green winter lawns. *Evergreen* is the
share of 1 ft pixels in a window with brightness-adjusted NDVI above %s, the same threshold
used to measure evergreen surroundings for holly candidates (plain NDVI is inflated in shadow;
see the [holly page](03_holly_classification.qmd#shadows)); open water is excluded. The forest-only line
uses the same measure within NLCD forest (classes 41–43) and reads as the evergreen
share of the forest canopy. NLCD forest cover is shown for reference.",
cfg$holly$thresholds$ndvi_adj$context))
```

```{r ndvi-plot, eval=!is.null(ndvi)}
nd <- left_join(ndvi, select(nlcd, window, forest_pct), by = "window")
evg_col <- "#01665e"
plot_ly(nd, x = ~u_mid_km) |>
  add_trace(y = ~evg_pct, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers", name = "Evergreen, all land",
            line = list(color = evg_col, width = 2), marker = list(color = evg_col, size = 8),
            hovertemplate = "Evergreen, all land: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>") |>
  add_trace(y = ~evg_forest_pct, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
            name = "Evergreen, within forest",
            line = list(color = evg_col, width = 2, dash = "dash"),
            marker = list(color = evg_col, size = 8, symbol = "circle-open"),
            hovertemplate = "Evergreen, within forest: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>") |>
  add_trace(y = ~forest_pct, type = "scatter", mode = "lines", name = "NLCD forest cover",
            line = list(color = "#38814e", width = 1.5, dash = "dot"),
            hovertemplate = "NLCD forest: %{y:.1f}%<extra></extra>") |>
  layout(xaxis = c(x_axis, list(hoverformat = ".1f")),
         yaxis = list(title = "Percent", range = c(0, 100), ticksuffix = "%"),
         hovermode = "x unified",
         legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2),
         annotations = landmarks, shapes = list(river_line),
         margin = list(t = 40)) |>
  plotly_cfg()
```

Evergreen cover follows the urban-to-forest gradient only loosely. It is lowest in downtown
Richmond (about 7–9% at km 0–2), sits between about 12% and 22% through most of the
transect, and peaks at 43% at km 21–22, where pine stands are common. In the developed
windows part of the signal is green winter lawn and street trees rather than evergreen canopy;
the adjusted index is calibrated on forest, so it is least reliable on bright urban surfaces.

Within forest the evergreen share does not follow the urban gradient. The small forest
patches near km 9–11 are pine-rich (41–46% evergreen), the forests at km 12–20 are mostly
deciduous (18–28%), km 21–22 is pine-rich again (54%), and km 23–24 is hardwood-dominated
(about 19%). The *amount* of forest (NLCD) and its *composition* (NDVI) change at different
places along the transect. That matters for holly: an isolated evergreen crown is easiest to
see, and most likely to be holly, in deciduous forest. Windows 1–4 have no NLCD forest, so
they have no forest-only value.

### Window table

```{r table}
nlcd |>
  transmute(Window = window,
            `Distance (km)` = sprintf("%.1f–%.1f", u_start_km, u_end_km),
            `Impervious (%)` = round(imperv_mean, 1),
            `Developed (%)` = round(developed_pct + developed_open_pct, 1),
            `Forest (%)` = round(forest_pct, 1),
            `Wetland (%)` = round(wetland_pct, 1),
            `Water (%)` = round(water_pct, 1)) |>
  left_join(if (is.null(ndvi)) data.frame(Window = integer()) else
              transmute(ndvi, Window = window, `NDVI mean` = round(ndvi_mean, 2),
                        `Evergreen (%)` = round(evg_pct, 1)),
            by = "Window") |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Notes

- **Data:** Annual NLCD Collection 1, `r cfg$nlcd$year` land cover (`LndCov`) and fractional
  impervious surface (`FctImp`), read for the AOI bounding box from the USGS web coverage
  service (`r cfg$nlcd$wcs_url`). No resampling or reprojection of the rasters.
- **Developed** combines NLCD classes 22–24 (low, medium, high intensity). Developed open
  space (21) is mostly lawns, parks, and road verges and is kept separate. **Forest** is
  classes 41–43; **wetland** is 90 and 95.
- **NDVI:** computed at full 1 ft resolution from the 4-band VBMP tiles and summarized into
  10 ft cells (mean NDVI and share of pixels above the evergreen threshold) before the window
  summaries. NLCD is resampled to the 10 ft grid (nearest neighbour) only to mask water and
  select forest. The NIR band is not radiometrically calibrated, so NDVI values are relative to
  this imagery, and leaf-off timing means NDVI says little about deciduous canopy.
- **Windows are not replicated samples.** Adjacent windows are spatially autocorrelated, so
  the curves describe the gradient but should not be treated as 25 independent observations.
- The 4 km width averages across very different ground on either side of the line (e.g. the
  James River crossing near 5–7 km). A narrower center band would test how much that matters.
